subject: Television & Streaming
title: The Five-Act Structure of Network TV
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Five-Act Structure of Network TV.

hook.text: Network dramas are written in five acts separated by commercial breaks.

discovery.text: This constraint shaped how television stories are told. Rising action, mini-climax, commercial break, repeat.

twist.text: Streaming shows have no act breaks. Writers can build tension continuously without interruption.

climax.text: The five-act structure is television's most invisible constraint.

punchline.text: Television drama was literally shaped by the need to sell soap.

quiz.question: How do commercial breaks affect the structure of network television writing?
options: Writers must build each act to a hook strong enough to keep viewers through the commercial break
